subject: Only getting 6 days of data in part 5 instead of 7 (missing the final day)

messages.author: d4b22285b2029fee
messages.subject: Only getting 6 days of data in part 5 instead of 7 (missing the final day)
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I'm new to this group so I hope this is posted in the right place etc, please accept my apologies if not. I am also new to GGIR and R but using it for my PhD and i've run into an issue, in that I am getting 6 days of valid data in part 5 instead of 7; I was wondering whether anyone could please help me to sort this out - it would be massively appreciated. 

For info, my ActiGraphs were set to record from midnight to midnight (recording time 7 days) and it always seems to miss off the final day of recording. To try and trouble shoot, I have been over the Part 2 Day summary and there are 7 days of recording on that output (although the final day seems to have a value of 23.75138889 for N Valid Hours for all participants (despite nearly every other day has 24 hours) 

Here is the part of the script i assume deals with the number of days of data etc: 
strategy = 1, hrs.del.start = 0,    hrs.del.end = 0,  
   ndayswindow = 7,  maxdur = 25,           includedaycrit = 16, qwindow=c(0,24),
  
Can anyone please point me in the right direction to help? I am happy to provide any other information that would be helpful. 

Thanks so much 

Aiden

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Only getting 6 days of data in part 5 instead of 7 (missing the final day)
parts:
Hi Aiden,

This is expected behavior from GGIR. GGIR only estimates sleep for 'nights' where there is at least a midnight timestamp in the data. The last midnight in your data is missing, by which GGIR assumes that sleep onset time cannot be reliably estimated. This in turn makes using the last measurement day questionable because we do not know when it's waking hours ended.

We could adapt or trick the algorithm to include the last day, but I am not sure that is a good idea. However, if you have good reasons to expect that most of your participants fall a sleep long before 23:45 then it seems justifiable to try to develop a work around.

This requires additional development work on GGIR, which I am afraid I can only do as a part of a paid consultancy. Let me know if you want to discuss this.

Best wishes,

Vincent
